pipelineLogs.message: Shot_14: One apparently frictionless route becomes an interdependent system whose flawless operation remains a requirement. An uncounted field of abstract session strips reveals the breadth of that requirement, not evidence of performance.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  A seemingly simple online voting conduit expands into a dependency loom, exposing the operational complexity of cryptography at population scale without claiming successful operation.
COMPOSITION  Render 1920x1080 at 60fps for 552 frames in light mode. Place a 1760x860 spatial stage below a compact top-left headline, 'Complexity expands,' and kicker, 'Illustrative system model.' Begin with the preceding method slabs stepping into shallow background layers above one broad neutral conduit. Unfold exactly eight large dependency pills: Input and Session at left; Proof method and Credential method vertically separated at center; Checking and Record at right; Deployment and Support across the bottom. Spacious curved routes weave through the central junction, using clear gaps at crossings. The loom, not an individual card, dominates the composition.
CAMERA  Use <mg.CameraRig> with a screen-fixed headline and kicker. Open at 100%, revealing the inherited slabs and simple conduit through a gentle lateral drift. As W274–W275 unfold the loom, reframe toward its center. Across W277–W278, push to 125% on the crowded junction, completing by frame 269. At W279–W280, track across the two cryptography pills without exceeding 125%. Across W284–W285, follow the neutral tile left to right through the inspection apertures; end the inspection stop with controlled ease-out by frame 435. Across W287–W289, pull back to 100% and pan right to left toward the upstream source, completing by frame 509. During frames 510–551, continue a subtle sourceward drift as the upstream inspection rule broadens into the boundary for the next shot.
TYPE  Use a crisp broadcast grotesk: 48px compact headline, 22px kicker, and 28–32px pill labels. Keep system labels subordinate to the paths and readable at the widest view. On W270, introduce the stage caption 'Simple online voting system,' completed by W273. Retire that caption as the loom unfolds. On W284–W285, reveal 'Requirement: flawless operation' beside the empty apertures, fully visible by frame 435. Do not typeset a population number or turn 'millions' into a metric.
COLOR/LIGHT  Use a porcelain-to-cool-gray multi-stop background with a soft ivory radial spotlight. Navy typography and slate paths provide contrast; coral is reserved for the tile corner, inspection frame, and upstream boundary. Use gentle paper-like shadows and faint texture. No teal checked state, dark-mode excursion, or alarm-red wash.
ELEMENTS  Eight ivory dependency pills with navy labels and restrained depth shadows; structural arrivals use spring damping 14, stiffness 160. · Broad initial conduit carrying the recurring small ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner. Keep it neutral throughout. · Curved navy-gray dependency paths with distinct crossings and small directional ticks; record activity travels left to right. Do not imply consensus or a specified voting protocol. · Three empty inspection apertures along the packet route, with a thin coral <mg.FocusFrame> identifying the active inspection area. No aperture fills or success indicators. · An uncounted field of low-contrast session strips beneath all eight nodes, distributed in bands rather than enumerated rows. · Multi-stop pale gradient, radial spotlight behind the junction, subtle <mg.GridBackground>, fine <mg.Noise>, and sparse architectural <mg.Marker> crosshairs. · Inherited thin baseline and coral frame; no illustrative SVG, giant numerical backdrop, or <mg.Roll> counter.
WORD SYNC  W267 → At frame 2, begin the neutral conduit's spring arrival beneath the inherited method slabs; make its leading edge visible by frame 7.
           W268 → By frame 30, settle the conduit and ivory tile while the inherited slabs recede into shallow system layers.
           W270 → Frames 46–67: isolate the single broad route with the coral focus frame, emphasizing apparent simplicity.
           W273 → Complete 'Simple online voting system' by frame 135; retain one route and one neutral tile.
           W274 → Frames 145–163: begin the conduit's branching transformation and spring the first dependency pills outward.
           W275 → By frame 180, reveal and settle all eight pills and their interdependent routes. Keep 'Illustrative system model' visible.
           W277 → Frames 189–230: begin the selective camera push and narrow the coral frame around the busiest junction.
           W278 → By frame 269, reach 125% zoom with separated curved paths, crossing gaps, and the junction fully legible.
           W279 → Frames 272–312: glide the inspection frame between Proof method and Credential method; reveal no proof output or completed credential.
           W280 → By frame 337, settle the camera with both cryptography pills and their adjoining dependencies in view.
           W284 → Frames 382–396: start linear left-to-right tile travel through the first empty inspection aperture and introduce 'Requirement:'.

AVOID  Decorative object SVGs, phone or ballot-box illustrations, and another slab-dossier composition. · Invented protocol details, hashes, voter identities, readable candidate choices, or implied person-to-vote linkage. · Population counters, enumerated session totals, performance metrics, outages, fabricated tests, or numerical ghost typography. · Green checks, filled inspection apertures, guaranteed privacy, verified consent, or any suggestion that flawless operation has been achieved. · An illegible hairball, excessive glow, camera scale above 130%, and unsynchronized primary reveals. · Depicting a particular voter as coerced or anticipating the next sentence's argument.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_15: A physical boundary interrupts a potential sightline, not the entire problem of coercion. Honor the film-wide SVG restriction by constructing the booth-like cutaway from tilted cards, planes, and rules rather than an illustrative object SVG. Its sheltered interior contrasts with the exposed viewing surface of the following shot.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Make physical separation tangible: an illustrative polling-station boundary sits between the voting tile and a hypothetical outside source of pressure, without implying that every form of coercion is prevented.
COMPOSITION  Render 1920x1080 at 60fps for 584 frames. Use a light editorial dossier stage, 1760x850, centered below a compact top-left headline. Match-cut the previous inspection rule into a broad separation plane. Place the sheltered working area and recurring vote tile on the right, an anonymous outside occupancy card on the left, and a monumental partition between them. Keep both regions connected by the inherited thin baseline. Small footer: 'Illustrative spatial model'.
CAMERA  Use one continuous <mg.CameraRig>, constrained to 100–125%. Begin at 100% with the inherited rule and both spatial zones visible. Push toward the boundary to 110% across W294–W296, easing into an inspection stop by f159. During W302–W303, pull to 100% as the cutaway assembles. Across W305–W306, push along the closing panel edge to 120%, finishing by f400. Across W307–W310, track right to left from the interior tile toward the outside occupancy card, exposing the intervening structure. Return to 100% by W316 f529. Through f583, continue only a subtle lateral drift that aligns the desk edge, vote tile, baseline, and coral focus frame for the next shot; retain the complete boundary in view.
TYPE  Use navy grotesk typography with compact uppercase utility labels. Headline begins as 'A BIGGER PROBLEM', with its final phrase revealed across W294–W295; replace it with 'COERCION' during W296 and settle by f159. Reveal 'POLLING STATION' over the interior during W302–W303. Reveal 'PHYSICAL SEPARATION' beside the panel across W305–W306, complete by f400. During W311, add the small qualifier 'Hypothetical pressure' near the outside card. Keep typography flat, readable, and clear of the cutaway.
COLOR/LIGHT  Warm ivory #F6F3EC through pale blue-gray #E8EEF2, navy #14283E typography, and restrained coral #E76F61 only at the separation edge and inspection contact. Soft upper-right radial illumination, shallow layered shadows, low-opacity grid and noise. Remain light throughout; no teal success coding.
ELEMENTS  <mg.GridBackground> beneath a warm ivory multi-stop gradient, soft radial spotlight, fine <mg.Noise>, and four restrained <mg.Marker> registration crosses. · Ten graphic primitives form the spatial cutaway: floor card, rear plane, two side planes, desk card, inner inset, two panel-edge rules, and two anonymous occupancy cards. No anatomy, faces, or pictograms. · The recurring small ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner rests on the interior desk card; no teal verification state or checkmark. · A thin coral inspection line extends rightward from the outside card and ends flush against the separation plane. A restrained <mg.FocusFrame> brackets that contact point. · A faint 900px ghost numeral '02' identifies only the two visible spatial zones, reinforced by small labels 'INTERIOR' and 'OUTSIDE'; it is not an election statistic.
WORD SYNC  W290 → At f2, spring the inherited inspection rule and interior vote tile into view using damping 14, stiffness 160. Complete their entrance by f24.
           W294 → Across f54–72, widen the inspection rule into the initial separation plane and reveal 'BIGGER'. Begin the motivated boundary push.
           W295 → Across f69–134, complete the broad boundary and headline 'A BIGGER PROBLEM'. Preserve generous negative space around the plane.
           W296 → Across f131–159, replace the headline with 'COERCION', illuminate the coral panel-edge accent, and ease the camera into its 110% inspection stop. Sustain restrained atmospheric drift through the spoken pause.
           W299 → Across f227–246, settle the recurring vote tile onto the interior working area and reveal its anonymous occupancy card. Keep the tile unverified.
           W302 → Across f262–285, spring in the floor, rear plane, and desk card. Start the contextual pullback and reveal 'POLLING'.
           W303 → Across f284–312, finish the inner inset, side planes, edge rules, and 'POLLING STATION' label; reach 100% camera scale. Leave the near side plane slightly offset for the separation demonstration.

AVOID  Object SVGs in this shot; use editorial planes and cards to respect the film-wide illustration restriction. · Locks, shields, checks, or language claiming that polling stations eliminate coercion. · Faces, human anatomy, real identities, readable candidate choices, or an identified coercer. · A coral line crossing the partition or a vote tile changing as if manipulated. · Camera scale above 130%, fabricated metrics, rolling population counters, or repeated network-mesh composition. · Dark-mode transition inside this shot, floating-point timing triggers, or substitution of local word indices.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_16: An exposed viewing surface replaces the sheltered voting space. A clear sightline makes the hypothetical pressure understandable without depicting a person, revealing a vote, or claiming a documented incident.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Expose the hypothetical risk of voting on an observable screen at home: protecting the record does not establish privacy or freedom from pressure. Preserve the supplied narration exactly.
COMPOSITION  1920x1080, 60fps, 634 frames. A 1760x860 dark inspection stage occupies approximately 73% of the canvas. Reserve top-left for the compact headline 'Who can see?' and kicker 'Hypothetical condition.' An oversized oblique desktop display and shallow keyboard dominate the lower-right field. A small anonymous source marker sits upper-left of the display, behind its viewing position; an unobstructed coral sightline connects them. Match-cut the previous desk plane, thin baseline, ivory vote tile, and coral inspection frame, but omit the protective booth panel.
CAMERA  Use one continuous <mg.CameraRig>. Start at zoom 1.55 on the inherited tile and desk-plane junction; frame 3 begins the schematic's structural arrival with spring damping 14, stiffness 160. Pull to 1.15 by W317 spokenEndFrame 11. Across W321–W322, pull to 1.00, revealing the full exposed setup by frame 114. During W327–W329, track right-to-left from the display edge back along the sightline toward its source while pushing to 1.25; settle by frame 272 in an observer-aligned POV, with no person or shoulder drawn. On W337, ease toward the display contact point at 1.30 by frame 482. On W338–W341, follow the reticle toward the opaque surface, then pull to 1.00 by frame 589. After the final spoken word, drift subtly toward 1.03 through frame 633, keeping both the source and screen visible.
TYPE  Use crisp ivory grotesk typography, a 48px headline, 22px kicker, and 36px callouts with generous spacing. Headline and kicker settle by W317's end. Reveal the first callout word-by-word on W332–W335 and the second on W338–W341, each word completing within its supplied spoken range. Keep both beside the source marker, never inside the display. Emphasize the second demand with a coral rule, not oversized warning typography.
COLOR/LIGHT  Use midnight navy #081321 through slate #172735 with a muted blue radial spotlight. Ivory #F4EFE5 defines the tile, type, and schematic edges; restrained coral #EE786E marks only the inspection route and unresolved exposure. Keep the display opaque matte blue-gray, never transparent or readable. Low-contrast grid, fine noise, soft card shadows, and separated foreground rules create broadcast-quality depth without neon bloom.
ELEMENTS  One clean eleven-element SVG schematic: screen shell, bezel, opaque display plane, stand, foot, desk plane, keyboard slab, and four neutral interface rules. Use restrained oblique geometry, not a detailed workstation illustration. · Recurring ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner, resting beside the screen foot as a continuity anchor. No teal verification state. · Anonymous <mg.Marker> at the sightline origin, labeled 'Possible observer'; no identity, silhouette, face, or occupancy claim. · Thin dashed coral sightline with a small linearly traveling inspection reticle; an open <mg.FocusFrame> brackets its contact with the display edge. · Two compact <mg.Card tilt={-2}> callouts beside the source marker: 'Vote for this candidate?' and 'show me your screen.' These represent the spoken hypothetical demands, not screen content. · Multi-stop midnight gradient, broad radial spotlight behind the display, faint <mg.GridBackground>, low-opacity <mg.Noise>, and sparse architectural corner markers.
WORD SYNC  W317 → At frame 3, spring in the screen assembly and compact headline. Resolve the inherited macro view to zoom 1.15 by spokenEndFrame 11; retain the previous baseline and coral inspection-frame alignment.
           W321 → Frames 82–98: begin the contextual pullback and bring the anonymous source marker into view; its entrance completes by frame 98.
           W322 → Frames 94–114: finish the pullback to 1.00 and reveal the unobstructed dashed route to the display edge. No booth panel, shield, or privacy barrier remains.
           W324 → Frames 156–184: an open coral inspection bracket settles around the empty stretch between source and screen, posing the question without asserting that safeguards never exist.
           W327 → Frames 217–244: track backward along the sightline toward its source, reaching zoom 1.12 by frame 244.
           W328 → Frames 241–263: continue into the observer-aligned viewpoint, reaching zoom 1.25 by frame 263 without introducing a human figure.
           W329 → Frames 260–272: finish the controlled ease-out inspection stop, holding the exposed viewing angle clearly.
           W331 → Frames 276–297: spring in the first empty callout card beside the source marker, ready for the quoted demand.
           W332 → Frames 343–358: reveal 'Vote' inside the source-side callout.
           W333 → Frames 355–366: append 'for' without moving the card.
           W334 → Frames 362–372: append 'this'; keep the display entirely abstract.
           W335 → Frames 370–396: complete 'Vote for this candidate?' No candidate name, choice, or ballot selection appears anywhere.
           W337 → Frames 457–482: soften the first callout, spring in a second empty card below it, and ease the camera to zoom 1.30 toward the display contact point.
           W338 → Frames 523–548: reveal 'show' and move the coral reticle linearly to the display edge, reaching it by frame 548.
           W339 → Frames 544–555: append 'me' as the camera begins its final contextual pullback.

AVOID  People, shoulders, hands, faces, domestic scenery, or a second illustrative object. · Readable candidate choices, real identities, invented hashes, or screen contents that reveal a vote. · Presenting the hypothetical observer as a confirmed coercer or depicting a documented incident. · Teal checks, locks, shields, or any implication that verified records establish privacy, consent, identity, or election-wide trust. · A transparent display, magnified ballot reveal, guaranteed receipt, or forced selection animation. · Local word-index substitutions, floating-point timestamps, late text reveals, fabricated counters, decorative ghost metrics, or a light-mode transition before the shot boundary.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_02: Matching abstract records propagate through selected model peers. A coral alteration interrupts one copy and exposes a comparison mismatch—not an invulnerable security shield. The final widening frame distinguishes the ledger network from the unrepresented conditions outside it. No illustrative entity SVG is needed.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Make the shared ledger feel seductively clear, then expose the boundary of what that clarity actually establishes: a visible record, not a trustworthy act of voting.
COMPOSITION  1920x1080, 60fps, frames 0–619. Place a 1760x850 light-mode network stage at x80, y170, occupying approximately 72% of the canvas. Reserve screen-space top-left for 'THE LEDGER PROMISE' and the kicker 'Illustrative record model'. Seven equal-weight ledger pills form a staggered, four-column mesh. Leave an airy perimeter outside the network boundary. Inherit the previous shot's vote tile, thin baseline, and coral frame alignment.
CAMERA  Use a continuous main <mg.CameraRig> constrained to zoom 1.00–1.26. Open with a clipped, node-local <mg.CameraRig zoom={1.6}> inspecting the inherited tile inside the first pill; resolve that local magnification to 1.00 by W24 end, f48, without enlarging the overall stage beyond its limit. Reveal the mesh footprint before W25. During W26, track left to right at zoom 1.14, following packets toward the first peers. Continue to the far-right peers during W28, reaching 1.20 by f258. From W29 through W34, reverse right to left toward the altered upstream copy, easing into inspection at 1.26. From W35 through W43, pull back to 1.00 and reframe the complete boundary by f578. Frames 579–619 retain a gentle leftward drift and scale push to 1.025, with no new primary reveal.
TYPE  Use a 48px navy headline, 22px kicker, 24px node labels, and 30px inspection callouts. Keep typography attached to the spatial stage except the headline and kicker. Reveal short labels with clean masks: 'VISIBLE RECORDS', then 'DISTRIBUTED COPIES', then 'MODEL MISMATCH'. Do not amplify 'Nobody' into an absolute-security slogan. Qualify the inspection with 'Changing a record: extremely difficult, not impossible.' Never roll statistics other than the visible model-node count.
COLOR/LIGHT  Warm ivory #F8F6F0 blends through pale blue-gray #EEF3F4 to #E1EAEE, with a broad white radial spotlight behind the mesh. Navy #13283E anchors text and structure; teal #187E7C denotes record-level matches only. Coral #E57164 appears sparingly at the tile corner, alteration stripe, and investigative boundary. Use 4% grid opacity, approximately 2% noise, soft card shadows, and a restrained coral frame glow. Keep the entire shot light mode.
ELEMENTS  Seven 360x160 glass-edged ledger pills, arranged one/two/two/two across the stage. Use <mg.Card tilt={-2}> for the entry pill and restrained floating shadows; keep record rows level and readable. · Recurring ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner. Preserve its inherited teal checked state strictly as record verification. Abstract rows contain only geometric bars: no candidate choices, identities, or fabricated hashes. · Curved bezier conduits with redundant cross-links. Teal packets move linearly left to right; peer cards have equal visual weight, with no master node or consensus-vote display. · <mg.Roll> labeled 'MODEL NODES' counts only cards actually revealed, from 1 to 7. Introduce a 900px ghost '07' at 3% opacity only once all seven demonstration nodes are visible. · A coral <mg.FocusFrame> first isolates one changed row, then widens into the network boundary. Teal matching rows remain unchanged elsewhere; the altered row loses its verified styling. · Multi-stop background gradient, radial spotlight, low-contrast <mg.GridBackground>, subtle <mg.Noise>, and architectural <mg.Marker> corner ticks provide layered spatial depth.
WORD SYNC  W23 → Trigger the inherited tile and first pill at W22 start +3 frames, f3. Use spring damping 14, stiffness 160, duration-bounded to settle by 'perfect,' f36. The tile docks on the inherited baseline.
           W24 → By f48, finish the compact headline and model kicker, resolve the node-local macro, and establish the entry pill as one peer rather than a central authority.
           W26 → During f107–152, linearly send packets into two spring-arriving peers while tracking right. Reveal identical abstract row patterns and 'VISIBLE RECORDS'; three model nodes are visible by f152.
           W28 → During f202–258, reveal the remaining four equal-weight peers and redundant routes. Packets continue left to right; matching rows, the count of 7, ghost '07', and 'DISTRIBUTED COPIES' are complete by f258.
           W29 → During f277–309, move the camera back toward an upstream peer and settle a coral inspection frame around one record row. Do not introduce locks, shields, or a network-wide approval state.
           W31 → During f323–354, expose a thin coral alteration stripe within the selected abstract row. Its verified styling is removed by f354.
           W32 → During f352–375, draw nondirectional comparison hairlines to unchanged neighboring rows and reveal 'MODEL MISMATCH'. These are inspection guides, not backward-traveling ledger packets.
           W34 → During f382–406, complete the restrained qualifier 'Changing a record: extremely difficult, not impossible.' Hold the mismatch as an illustrative comparison, not proof that every attack is detected.
           W35 → During f451–462, retire the local comparison label and release the inspection stop. Begin the system-wide pullback without cutting.
           W41 → During f504–543, expose the unoccupied perimeter and reveal 'OUTSIDE THE LEDGER' beyond the growing coral boundary. Add no people, threat icons, or claims about a particular voter.
           W43 → During f547–578, finish the wide coral frame around all seven peers and settle the main camera at 1.00. Keep the source-side vote tile and baseline clearly available for the next comparison-board match cut.
AVOID  Decorative object SVGs, portraits, fingerprints, locks, shields, or blockchain logos. · Readable ballot choices, real identities, invented hashes, election metrics, or performance claims. · Treating teal checks as identity, privacy, consent, anonymity, or whole-election verification. · Absolute immutability, guaranteed attack detection, or seven peers implying unanimous network control. · Right-to-left transaction packets, bouncy inspection stops, dark-mode treatment, or cluttered subtitles.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_17: Two adjacent fields expose the boundary between checking a record and protecting a voluntary act. A teal pulse stays inside the record window; a separate dashed coral route crosses the boundary as a possible misuse pathway. The coercion bracket never closes.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  A locally verified voting record and unresolved coercion remain visible together: digital verifiability could create a misuse pathway without solving the conditions around the voter.
COMPOSITION  Render 1920x1080 at 60fps for 422 frames. Return to light mode on a 1760x870 comparison stage centered at x960, y605, occupying approximately 74% of the canvas. Reserve the top-left for the compact headline 'Record ≠ consent'. Two floating <mg.Card> panels, each 700x810, sit at x180 and x1040 with a 160px coral-accented gutter; use tilt={-2} and tilt={2}. Left: 'digitally verifiable', an oversized abstract record-view window, the recurring vote tile, and 'Illustrative record model'. Right: 'coercion', a neutral viewing-surface crop made from rectangular layers, an external source marker, the inherited sightline, and an open condition bracket. Keep a thin baseline continuous beneath both cards. No new illustrative SVG.
CAMERA  Use continuous <mg.CameraRig> movement between zoom 1.00 and 1.30. Begin at zoom 1.30 focused on the inherited right-hand condition bracket. From W342 through W345, ease outward to 1.18, revealing the viewing surface while leaving the bracket unchanged. Across W346–W347, pull to 1.00 to establish both cards. Starting W348, track right to left toward the vote tile, reaching a selective 1.23 inspection view by W351's end; drift gently to 1.25 through W352. Across W353–W354, pull to 1.05 and reframe toward the external marker. On W355–W356, track right to left along the dashed route toward the record window, reaching 1.14 with a controlled ease-out stop by frame 377. Frames 378–411 pull to 1.00; maintain a barely perceptible lateral drift through frame 421. Keep the headline outside the rig and prevent either card from clipping during the final wide view.
TYPE  Use crisp navy editorial sans-serif, a 44px compact headline, 40px card labels, and 24px model/path captions. Start the right card's structural arrival at frame 3 using spring damping 14, stiffness 160; settle its primary reveal by frame 25. The headline resolves by W345's end. Establish card labels during the contextual pullback, then emphasize 'digitally' and 'verifiable' separately on their aligned cues. Introduce 'Possible' on W353 and complete 'Possible misuse pathway' by W355's end. No text scramble, fabricated counters, or oversized decorative numerals.
COLOR/LIGHT  Light-mode palette: warm ivory #F5F2EA through pale blue-gray #E9EFF2, navy #15283E typography, coral #E66F61 fault lines, and restrained teal #25897E only for record correspondence. Use a broad radial white spotlight behind the panels, grid at approximately 5% opacity, noise at 2%, and soft layered shadows. Keep the coral route distinct from the teal record check; never wash the stage in either status color.
ELEMENTS  Multi-stop ivory gradient, soft radial spotlight, low-contrast <mg.GridBackground>, subtle <mg.Noise>, and architectural <mg.Marker> registration points. · Two large <mg.Card> panels with restrained tilt, fine navy borders, soft lifted shadows, and a coral fault-line gutter. · Abstract record-view window with neutral rules and placeholders only; no readable choices, identities, hashes, or election metrics. · Recurring small ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner. Its localized teal checked state denotes correspondence with the illustrative record only. · Right-hand neutral viewing-surface crop, anonymous external marker, thin sightline, and visibly open condition bracket; no device silhouette or person. · Dashed coral inspection path and a glowing <mg.FocusFrame> spanning the gutter, labeled 'Possible misuse pathway'. · Persistent thin baseline and an understated open continuation rail for the next claim-audit stage.
WORD SYNC  W342 → Frames 3–25: spring the right-hand condition field into its inherited position; begin the close-up camera reveal. Preserve the external sightline and open bracket.
           W343 → Frames 22–37: briefly brighten the existing coral bracket ends without joining them.
           W344 → Frames 33–51: settle the bracket emphasis; introduce no repair, closure, checkmark, or security seal.
           W345 → Frames 47–60: finish the contextual reframe at zoom 1.18 and resolve 'Record ≠ consent'. The condition remains visibly unchanged.
           W346 → Frames 101–110: initiate the wider comparison reveal; extend the baseline toward the left record card.
           W347 → Frames 111–130: complete the two-card reveal at zoom 1.00, including both labels and 'Illustrative record model'.
           W348 → Frames 147–172: lift the record-view window with the structural spring and begin the right-to-left inspection move.
           W349 → Frames 168–178: reveal a single empty correspondence slot inside the illustrative record window.
           W350 → Frames 174–191: move the recurring vote tile linearly left to right into that slot; keep its navy mark and clipped coral corner legible.
           W351 → Frames 189–219: emphasize 'digitally' and complete the camera's selective record-window push to zoom 1.23.
           W352 → Frames 215–257: emphasize 'verifiable'; run one contained teal correspondence pulse and settle the tile's checked record state. Do not color the whole card or baseline teal.
           W353 → Frames 274–292: reveal 'Possible' beside the external marker and initiate the dashed coral route; begin widening toward its origin.
           W354 → Frames 288–304: finish the origin reframe at zoom 1.05; extend the route to the gutter while the <mg.FocusFrame> expands across it.
           W355 → Frames 306–339: follow the coral route right to left across the gutter. Complete 'Possible misuse pathway' and lightly emphasize the right-card label; leave its bracket open.
           W356 → Frames 348–377: finish the dashed trace at the abstract record-window edge and ease the camera to its inspection stop. Pause the coral frame around the route without revealing a choice or converting the pathway into a confirmed event.
AVOID  New illustrative SVG, device silhouettes, people, ballot-box icons, or decorative object drawings. · Treating a checked record as verified identity, privacy, consent, anonymity, or election integrity. · Showing actual coercion, an identified victim, a guaranteed ballot receipt, or a readable voting choice. · Closing the coercion bracket or presenting the dashed route as inevitable. · Invented hashes, performance figures, election totals, or rolling counters. · Comparing storage with identity instead of record verifiability with a possible human consequence. · Camera scale above 1.30, abrupt camera reversals, or cuts inside the spoken line. · Reintroducing dark mode, the previous desktop hero, or the next shot's attributed hacking claim.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_18: A query becomes evidence under inspection. The claim remains visibly attributed while a coral trace connects its absolute wording to a precise correction. This is an editorial audit, not a security simulation. No illustrative entity SVG is needed.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Inspect an attributed absolute claim about blockchain security, then attach the spoken correction without implying a breach or demonstrating an attack.
COMPOSITION  1920x1080, 60fps, 542 frames. Light-mode claim-audit workbench: a 1760x850 spatial stage centered at x960/y595 occupies approximately 72% of the canvas. Reserve the top-left for the compact headline 'Cyber security'. Inside the stage, place a broad input field above three cascading 1600px-wide trace cards: attribution, quoted claim, and response. Use shallow stepped offsets and <mg.Card tilt={-2}> on the foreground response. Keep the attributed claim and its attached 'Claim' tab readable when the response advances. Inherit the previous shot's ivory vote tile, thin navy baseline, and coral <mg.FocusFrame>; park the tile at the input rail's left edge without introducing a new verification state.
CAMERA  Use <mg.CameraRig> for one continuous, legible investigation move. At W357, start at zoom 1.0 with the inherited tile and baseline aligned to the previous shot; ease into a subtle contextual drift. W360–W361 opens the stacked stage. W362–W364 selectively reframe toward the attribution and input. As W365–W366 type, push toward zoom 1.12 while following the text reveal left to right. On W367, reach zoom 1.25 and center the coral reticle on 'impossible'; track gently toward the sentence ending through W368, then ease to a clean inspection stop by W369's spokenEndFrame. Hold the full attribution within view. On W370, begin pulling back as the response advances. By W372's spokenEndFrame, return to zoom 1.0 with the complete correction visibly connected to the claim. During the remaining hold, drift right to left and lower the framing toward the open continuation rail. Never exceed zoom 1.25.
TYPE  Use a precise modern sans serif: headline 46px, attribution 44px, claim and input 66px, correction 78px, structural labels 24px. Navy text on ivory; coral identifies inspection, not danger spectacle. Reveal 'Cyber' on W360 and 'security' on W361. Build the attribution word by word on W362–W364. After attribution is complete, type 'Blockchain is impossible to hack.' character by character into the input and mirror each character simultaneously into the quoted-claim strip. Each word finishes by its own global cue's spokenEndFrame; during overlapping cues, finish the preceding word before displaying the next. Keep the 'Claim' tab attached throughout. Reveal the correction as 'That's' on W370, 'not' on W371, and 'true.' on W372. Do not strike out, replace, or erase the original attributed claim.
COLOR/LIGHT  Use warm ivory #F6F3EC, pale blue-gray #E7EDF1, and white card faces over a soft multi-stop gradient. Navy #142B42 carries text and rails; restrained coral #E77769 carries the inspection reticle and correction connector. Subtle spotlighting, fine grain, and broad low-opacity card shadows create depth without darkening the scene. No teal security verdict, alarm red wash, or neon effects.
ELEMENTS  Warm ivory multi-stop background gradient with a soft radial spotlight behind the workbench, low-contrast <mg.GridBackground>, fine <mg.Noise>, and sparse architectural <mg.Marker> crosshairs. · Oversized input field with a structural 'Claim' tab attached before any quoted text appears. Reserve fixed text positions to prevent typing-induced reflow. · Three floating trace cards with restrained shadows: source strip 'People often say,', quoted-claim strip 'Blockchain is impossible to hack.', and response strip 'That's not true.'. Reveal each only with its assigned word cues. · A giant ghost question mark, fontSize 900 and approximately 3% opacity, behind the stage; keep it subordinate to the readable claim. · Coral <mg.FocusFrame> inspection reticle, a thin response-to-claim connector, and an open continuation rail along the lower edge. · Recurring small ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner. It is a continuity anchor, not evidence of identity, consent, privacy, or election security.
WORD SYNC  W357 → Begin the hero workbench entrance at local frame 3 using spring damping 14 and stiffness 160. Bring in the inherited tile and baseline immediately; complete the initial visible entrance by W357's spokenEndFrame, with only residual settling afterward.
           W360 → Reveal 'Cyber' and spring the trace-card stack into its first shallow stepped arrangement; the source, claim, and response surfaces are visible but their narration-dependent text remains empty.
           W361 → Complete the headline 'Cyber security' and the stack's expanded geometry. Stabilize card edges and preserve the open lower rail.
           W362 → Reveal 'People' in the source strip and begin the selective camera reframe toward the attribution.
           W363 → Append 'often' to the source strip without moving the already revealed word.
           W364 → Append 'say,' to complete 'People often say,'. Settle the attribution above the empty quoted-claim strip; its 'Claim' tab remains attached.
           W365 → Type 'Blockchain' character by character into the input and mirrored claim strip. Begin the continuous camera push and left-to-right reading follow.
           W366 → Append ' is' in both locations and reach zoom 1.12.
           W367 → Append ' impossible'. Reach zoom 1.25 and ease the coral inspection reticle around that word only; retain the visible attribution and 'Claim' tab.
           W368 → Append ' to' after the preceding word finishes and gently follow toward the sentence ending without moving the reticle off 'impossible'.
           W369 → Append ' hack.' to complete the exact quoted sentence in both locations. Finish the camera's controlled ease-out inspection stop.
           W370 → Spring the response strip forward with damping 14 and stiffness 160, reveal 'That's', and start the wide pullback. Draw the first section of a coral connector toward the inspected claim.
           W371 → Append ' not' and complete the thin coral connector from the response to the claim's inspected wording.

AVOID  Exploit code, broken shields, padlocks, hacker silhouettes, breach animation, or decorative illustrative SVGs. · Presenting 'Blockchain is impossible to hack.' without its visible attribution and attached 'Claim' tab. · Invented attack metrics, hashes, readable candidate choices, voter identities, performance counters, or blanket security guarantees. · Treating a teal record-verification state as verification of the voter or the whole election. · Another transaction-history table or dual comparison board; retain the distinct cascading query-and-inspection family. · Camera zoom above 1.25, abrupt whip moves, illegible perspective, text reflow, or premature correction text. · Floating-point timestamps, substituted local word indices, duplicated narration, or transitions outside the assigned shot.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_19: A protected subsystem inside a larger, incompletely inspected perimeter. The ledger is only one destination for activity arriving from other components; its resistance to alteration does not certify those sources. No illustrative entity SVG is needed: use cards, pills, paths, abstract rows, and a traveling focus frame.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Concede the ledger's resistance to alteration, then expose its limited boundary within a larger election system. Record protection does not establish protection of every component.
COMPOSITION  1920x1080, 60fps, 511 frames, light mode. Build a 1760x860 spatial stage centered beneath a compact top-left headline, 'Ledger ≠ whole system'. Arrange seven nodes around an open inspection field: one dominant ledger slab at the right and six broad, unlabeled component pills in separate upstream branches above, below, and left. Use curved, non-crossing conduits directed toward the ledger. Label the stage 'Illustrative system model' and its abstract ledger inset 'Illustrative record model'. Preserve generous central negative space for the coral inspection aperture.
CAMERA  Use one continuous <mg.CameraRig>. Open at zoom 1.5 on the ledger's retained row and matched continuation rail; begin the hero slab's spring arrival at frame 2 with damping 14 and stiffness 160. Ease to 1.25 by W377 frame 147, establishing the ledger's local context. During W378–W381, make a restrained tracking move with the proposed-edit layer and settle at its inspection stop by frame 265. On W382, initiate a decisive right-to-left investigative move and pull to 1.0 by frame 311, revealing the wider perimeter. Continue a gentle leftward track through W385, then keep the complete seven-node architecture readable through frame 460. During frames 461–510, ease toward the upstream aperture and push to 1.12, positioning it to receive the next shot's application-window schematic.
TYPE  Use a premium grotesk with navy semibold labels and generous spacing. Keep the compact headline screen-fixed outside the rig. Reveal 'Ledger' at W377. Build the ledger callout sequentially as 'extremely', 'difficult', 'to', 'alter', completing each word by its aligned end frame; the final callout reads 'extremely difficult to alter'. Reveal the shared upstream heading 'Other components' across W388–W389 without naming individual pills. Model labels remain legible but subordinate. No decorative oversized numeral or counter: neither serves this argument.
COLOR/LIGHT  Ivory #F7F5EE, pale blue #E8EFF3, navy #172C40, and restrained coral #E87968. Give the ledger a cool radial highlight and shallow layered shadows; use coral only for the proposed edit, correspondence inspection, and traveling focus frame. Upstream components remain neutrally lit, not coded as breached or unsafe. No teal success treatment.
ELEMENTS  Warm ivory-to-pale-blue multi-stop background, a soft radial spotlight behind the ledger, low-opacity <mg.GridBackground>, fine <mg.Noise>, and sparse architectural <mg.Marker> crosshairs. · Right-edge ledger slab as a shallow floating <mg.Card tilt={-2}> with abstract unreadable rows, three downstream correspondence seams, and a thin baseline inherited from the previous shot. · Recurring ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner, retained inside one ledger row. Keep it neutral; do not imply voter or election verification. · Translucent coral proposed-edit layer that approaches the retained row without replacing it. Correspondence seams illuminate to suggest ramifications of an edit, not an impossible-to-cross barrier. · Six neutral upstream pills with restrained navy outlines. Their faint structural footprints can precede their full spring reveal; no names, identities, candidate choices, or invented hashes. · Separate small neutral packets traveling linearly along curved left-to-right routes toward the ledger. These demonstrate component connections, not consensus or measured throughput. · A softly glowing coral <mg.FocusFrame> that starts around the ledger row, then relocates to the upstream branches and becomes the next shot's application inspection aperture.
WORD SYNC  W373 → At frame 2, spring the ledger slab and retained vote tile into the opening macro composition; establish their readable state by frame 31. Match the previous shot's thin rail and coral inspection frame.
           W377 → Frames 117–147: resolve the 'Ledger' label and 'Illustrative record model' inset caption while the camera settles to zoom 1.25.
           W378 → Frames 169–210: reveal 'extremely' and bring the translucent coral proposed-edit layer toward the retained row. Light the first correspondence seam; stop short of replacing any content.
           W379 → Frames 206–234: reveal 'difficult' and illuminate the remaining correspondence seams, showing that an alteration would have linked consequences.
           W380 → Frames 232–241: reveal 'to' with a short opacity-and-position settle; keep the proposed edit visibly separate from the record.
           W381 → Frames 238–265: reveal 'alter' and complete the controlled inspection stop. Hold the proposal beside the unchanged row without a rejection cross, lock, or invulnerability effect.
           W382 → Frames 298–311: pivot the argument with a right-to-left pullback to zoom 1.0. Move the coral focus frame off the ledger and into the upstream inspection field.
           W384 → Frames 312–336: reveal the broad system perimeter, its six faint component footprints, and 'Illustrative system model'. Keep the ledger visibly contained within this larger architecture.
           W385 → Frames 334–364: finish the leftward contextual reframe and trace six distinct upstream conduits toward the right-edge ledger, avoiding a consensus-network layout.
           W387 → Frames 397–419: spring all six neutral pills from their faint footprints into full readable form using damping 14 and stiffness 160. Complete their structural arrival by frame 419.
           W388 → Frames 415–428: reveal 'Other' and expand the coral focus frame around the upstream branches. Launch separate neutral packets along the curved routes toward the ledger.
           W389 → Frames 426–460: complete 'Other components', settle the upstream focus frame, and finish the packets' linear route traversals by frame 460. Keep all seven nodes visible for the completed comparison.
AVOID  Locks, shields, impenetrable walls, absolute rejection symbols, or any suggestion that alteration is impossible. · Implying that a verified record proves identity, privacy, consent, or whole-election integrity. · Decorative object illustrations, consensus meshes, repeated transaction tables, or dependency-loom layouts. · Readable candidate choices, real voter identities, invented hashes, fabricated metrics, and unnecessary rolling counters. · Labeling upstream components as compromised or previewing the next sentence's specific vulnerabilities. · Right-to-left ledger packets, excessive glow, dark-mode treatment, or handheld camera motion. · Unaligned word emphasis, floating-point timing triggers, or primary reveals continuing beyond their spoken end frames.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_20: An opaque software surface becomes an inspectable stack: protecting its eventual record does not establish that its upstream conditions were trustworthy. The sole illustrative hero is a clean twelve-element application-window SVG, not a phone, desktop, or real interface. Open coral brackets identify questions, never confirmed breaches.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Expose four potential weaknesses upstream of the ledger without depicting an actual compromise. The recurring vote tile remains neutral while inspection moves through device access, host, application, and identity layers.
COMPOSITION  1920x1080, 60fps, 585 frames. Build a 1760x850 light-mode dossier stage with a dominant 1240x730 exploded application-window schematic. Reserve the top-left for the compact headline 'Before the record' and kicker 'Potential exposure points'. Four oversized inspection tabs connect to separate schematic layers; keep labels legible throughout camera movement. Match the incoming upstream aperture, thin baseline, and coral focus frame. Label the stage 'Illustrative application model'.
CAMERA  Use one continuous <mg.CameraRig>. Begin with a 150% POV macro on the incoming aperture and ivory tile; pull back across f2–29 to a 100% contextual view of the schematic, keeping the stage's outer labels off until the reveal. From W391 through W394, push to 108% on the right access edge. From W395 through W399, track right to left and downward, reaching 114% at the host layer. From W400 through W405, continue toward the exposed content seam and reach 120%. From W406 through W411, track farther left to the lifted authentication plane while easing back to 100%; all four tabs and brackets are visible by f528. Inspection stops use controlled ease-out. During f529–584, maintain a subtle push toward 103% and reframe the unchanged tile toward the next shot's source position. No hard cut inside the narration.
TYPE  Use a precise navy grotesk: headline 44px, inspection labels 36–40px, model caption 22px. Tabs enter with spring damping 14 and stiffness 160; settle before their aligned noun ends. Add small qualifiers on the predicate cues: 'can be hacked', 'can be infected', 'can have vulnerabilities', and 'can be compromised'. Keep qualifiers attached to their labels so the modal language is never lost. Use coral for inspection rules, not alarm-red headlines. Avoid kinetic word-by-word transcript duplication.
COLOR/LIGHT  Keep this shot light: warm ivory #F5F2EB through cool pale blue #E7EEF2, navy #15283C typography, restrained coral #E8796B inspection accents. A broad white radial spotlight lifts the schematic; soft contact shadows distinguish exploded planes. Grid and noise remain barely visible. Use a restrained coral halo on the active bracket, never a warning strobe. No teal checks: nothing about the device, identity, consent, or vote has been verified.
ELEMENTS  Application-window SVG, exactly twelve elements: outer shell, header strip, three neutral header dots, opaque content plane, three neutral interface bands, input strip, session footer, and inset perimeter rule. Use restrained layer offsets and soft separation shadows. · Four floating <mg.Card tilt={-2}> inspection tabs: 'Your phone' at the right access edge, 'Your computer' beneath the host layer, 'Voting application' beside the content seam, and 'Identity system' at the lower-left authentication plane. Thin leader paths terminate at distinct open brackets. · Recurring ivory vote tile with a navy geometric mark and clipped coral corner, positioned within the opaque content plane. It stays unchanged and unchecked throughout. · One active coral <mg.FocusFrame> travels between inspection sites, leaving thin open bracket residues so all four potential exposure points remain visible at the end. · Multi-stop ivory background, broad radial spotlight, subtle <mg.GridBackground>, low-opacity <mg.Noise>, architectural <mg.Marker> crosshairs, and a giant ghost numeral '4' at fontSize 900 behind the final overview. The numeral counts inspection points, not election data.
WORD SYNC  W390 → At f2, begin the hero schematic's spring entrance through the inherited aperture, damping 14 and stiffness 160. Show the opaque plane and unchanged vote tile by f12; remaining structural settlement completes with W391.
           W391 → Spring in 'Your phone' and connect it to the outer access edge; complete the contextual reveal and label settlement by f29.
           W394 → Across W392–W394, reveal 'can be hacked' and ease the coral aperture onto the access edge. Finish the 108% inspection push by f66; leave the bracket open without damage or intrusion.
           W396 → Begin on W395 at f111. Spring in 'Your computer', reveal the lower host rule, and start the right-to-left camera track. Complete the tab and leader by f150.
           W399 → Across W397–W399, add 'can be infected' and settle the active bracket on the lower host layer. Finish the 114% inspection framing by f189; retain the first open bracket.
           W402 → Begin on W400 at f233. Reveal 'Voting application' and separate the opaque content plane slightly from the shell. Complete the label and structural lift by f296.
           W405 → Across W403–W405, reveal 'can have vulnerabilities', bracket the exposed application seam, and settle the camera at 120% by f361. Keep the tile fixed to the content plane and unchanged.
           W408 → Begin on W406 at f409. Reveal 'Identity system'; lift the session footer into a distinct authentication plane and connect its lower-left tab. Complete these reveals by f474.
           W411 → Across W409–W411, add 'can be compromised', place the fourth open bracket, and widen to 100%. Reveal the faint numeral '4' and finish the complete four-point overview by f528.
AVOID  Phone or computer object illustrations, decorative SVGs, recognizable operating-system interfaces, and more than twelve hero SVG elements. · Actual breach imagery, malware icons, altered vote marks, locked shields, success checks, or language asserting a confirmed compromise. · Candidate choices, real identities, invented hashes, fabricated metrics, or guaranteed privacy and security. · A repeated network mesh or comparison board; this shot's visual family is an exploded editorial software dossier. · Floating-point timing, substitute word indices, delayed primary reveals, excessive glitching, or an internal sentence cut.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_22: A two-sided information-boundary test: matching an incoming pattern to its stored representation does not resolve the separate correctness requirement upstream. Teal correspondence remains confined to the right-hand record pair; the source-side correctness bracket remains open, not failed.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Protecting a recorded pattern is distinct from establishing whether the incoming information was correct. Preserve the preceding hypothetical mismatch without implying that all inputs are wrong.
COMPOSITION  Render 1920x1080 at 60fps for 611 frames. Use a porcelain-light 1760x870 comparison stage, approximately 74% of the canvas, with two 700x810 floating cards separated by the inherited vertical ledger-entry boundary. Reserve the top-left for the compact headline 'The key distinction'. Left card: 'information entering the system', with oversized original-versus-altered geometric comparison slots, a persistent 'Hypothetical example' tab, and an empty bracket labeled 'Input correctness'. Right card: 'after it's recorded.', pairing the arriving altered vote tile with its retained abstract pattern; attach 'Illustrative record model' to this card only. Align both cards to the inherited thin baseline. Keep the ivory vote tile, navy geometric mark, clipped coral corner, and coral inspection frame visually continuous with the previous shot.
CAMERA  Use <mg.CameraRig> with continuous, motivated movement; remain within zoom 1.0–1.2. Open at zoom 1.2 on the inherited ledger boundary, match-cutting the tile, baseline, and coral frame. Begin the cards' structural entrance at frame 2 with spring damping 14 and stiffness 160. Pull to zoom 1.0 by W440's spokenEndFrame 64, exposing the complete light-mode comparison. From W441, selectively push toward the right card, reaching zoom 1.2 by W445's spokenEndFrame 213. Drift gently across the record pair through W450. Starting W451, track the coral frame right to left across the boundary, arriving over the unresolved source comparison by W453's spokenEndFrame 430 with controlled ease-out. Continue a shallow inspection pan toward the empty correctness bracket; stop precisely by W461's spokenEndFrame 565. Pull back to zoom 1.0 during frames 566–610, retaining both the right-hand match and the left-hand open requirement. Keep the correctness bracket prominent for the next shot's query-aperture match cut.
TYPE  Use a precise editorial sans serif: 42px compact headline, 32px card headings, and 22–24px supporting labels. Keep graphics dominant; no full-screen quotation or transcript crawl. Bring in 'The key distinction' with a short masked rise, settled by W440. Card headings arrive as structural context, with emphasis—not replacement text—locked to the corresponding spoken words. On W448–W450, underline 'after it's recorded.' locally. On W452–W453, give 'Input correctness' a restrained coral emphasis without adding a failure verdict. Keep all labels screen-readable during camera moves and retain the exact narration unchanged.
COLOR/LIGHT  Restore light mode immediately: porcelain #F6F3EC through cool ivory #EDF1F2, navy #14283B typography and geometry, restrained coral #E77969 for the boundary investigation, and muted teal #338D86 only for local record correspondence. Use a broad upper-right radial spotlight, delicate card elevation, fine grid lines, and barely perceptible procedural grain. Let the preceding dark palette survive only as a brief opening edge shadow, cleared by W440; never recolor the entire left card coral.
ELEMENTS  Two <mg.Card tilt={-2}> and <mg.Card tilt={1}> surfaces with restrained shadows, fine navy rules, generous spacing, and large geometric comparison windows. · Left comparison slots retain the faint original source pattern and altered incoming pattern from the preceding hypothetical example, joined by a thin coral discrepancy tether. Use abstract geometry, never candidate selections. · Right record pair contains the altered ivory vote tile and an identical retained pattern. A narrow teal scan resolves into local correspondence outlines and a small 'Recorded pattern matches input' label. · A vertical ledger-entry boundary and shared horizontal baseline organize the before-versus-after stage. Any traveling data motion runs left to right. · One coral <mg.FocusFrame> travels right to left for investigation, ultimately fitting the empty 'Input correctness' bracket rather than enclosing the entire left card. · Multi-stop porcelain gradient, broad radial spotlight, faint <mg.GridBackground>, low-opacity <mg.Noise>, and sparse architectural <mg.Marker> registration crosses. No illustrative entity SVG, counters, or decorative numerals.
WORD SYNC  W437 → At frame 2, begin the paired-card spring arrival and continuous return from the inherited dark boundary to porcelain light. Establish the ivory tile and thin baseline immediately.
           W440 → By frame 64, complete the opening pullback to zoom 1.0, settle both cards, and finish the headline reveal. The before-versus-after boundary is fully legible.
           W441 → From frame 106, begin the selective right-card push and reveal its local 'Illustrative record model' caption, fully readable by frame 138.
           W443 → During frames 144–167, initiate a narrow teal scan at the incoming pattern. Keep its leading edge inside the right card.
           W445 → By frame 213, reach zoom 1.2 and complete the linear left-to-right scan from arriving pattern to retained pattern. Resolve matching outlines around these two windows only.
           W447 → By frame 255, finish revealing 'Recorded pattern matches input' beneath the pair; any teal checked state applies only to this record correspondence.
           W448 → During frames 273–300, emphasize 'after' in the right heading with a thin underline beginning on the recorded side of the boundary.
           W450 → By frame 328, complete the underline beneath 'after it's recorded.' and settle the local correspondence treatment. Preserve this factual concession throughout the following investigation.
           W451 → At frame 374, activate the coral inspection frame at the right-card edge and begin the camera's return toward the source.
           W452 → During frames 380–401, move the coral frame across the ledger-entry boundary from right to left without erasing the teal record match.
           W453 → By frame 430, ease the frame into the unresolved source comparison. Keep 'Hypothetical example' visible and avoid any whole-card error treatment.
           W456 → By frame 481, complete a restrained emphasis pass across the original and altered geometric source patterns, preserving their existing discrepancy tether.
           W457 → During frames 483–513, trace the incoming-information rail left to right toward the ledger boundary while the inspection camera remains upstream.
           W459 → By frame 543, settle the rail highlight at the boundary and reframe the empty correctness bracket alongside the source comparison.
           W460 → During frames 540–551, contract the coral frame toward the empty 'Input correctness' bracket, leaving the hypothetical mismatch visible nearby.
           W461 → By frame 565, stop the frame precisely around the empty bracket. Add no check, cross, or verdict. All semantic reveals are complete before the final wide handoff.
AVOID  Camera zoom above 1.3 or crops that obscure the relationship between source, boundary, and record. · Illustrative object SVGs, locks, shields, people, decorative blockchains, or a third comparison card. · Teal checks implying verified identity, privacy, consent, input truth, or an entire election. · An error cross, red wash, or claim that every incoming record is incorrect. · Readable candidate choices, real identities, invented hashes, fabricated metrics, or claims of impossible record alteration. · Reversing data flow when the camera investigates right to left. · Premature next-shot query text, extra narration, floating-point timing triggers, or substituted local word indices.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_24: Transparency becomes physical inspectability: one retained paper source, approached through several distinct examination routes. Construct the stack from offset <mg.Card> planes rather than an illustrative SVG, preserving the film's restriction on additional object emblems. Clean rules, empty boxes, and layered paper edges provide the storyboard's iconic paper silhouette.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Present retained paper and multiple inspection routes as an illustrative transparency model, not a guarantee of election legitimacy or universal implementation. Preserve the supplied narration unchanged across 682 frames at 60fps.
COMPOSITION  Render 1920x1080 in light mode. A 1760x870 animated audit stage occupies approximately 74% of the canvas. Reserve the top-left for the compact headline 'Transparency' and kicker 'Illustrative transparency model,' revealed with W479. Center a monumental 1100x760 paper-audit stack slightly right within the stage. Five shallow procedural bands unfold around its perimeter without obscuring the sheets. Inherit the preceding goal plane, thin baseline, ivory vote tile, and coral inspection aperture; finish with the aperture positioned for the next label-to-evidence inspection stage.
CAMERA  Use one continuous <mg.CameraRig>, always between 100% and 115%. Open at 115% on the inherited goal plane and coral aperture; the paper stack begins entering at frame 2 with spring damping 14 and stiffness 160. From W480 through W486, pull to 100% to reveal the complete stage by frame 264. On W488–W489, push to 110% toward the retained sheet edges. Track the inspection band right to left on W490, then ease to a precise edge-registration stop on W491. On W492, follow a second right-to-left pass across the same paper source at 112%, ending by frame 499. From W493 through W496, pull to 100% while all five bands settle into view. After frame 634, maintain subtle lateral drift at 100% and move the coral aperture toward the naming-band position of the next shot.
TYPE  Use compact navy editorial sans-serif labels with generous tracking and no oversized sentence overlay. Set 'If the goal is transparency' on the inherited goal plane, revealing each word from W475–W479 and completing each by its spoken end. Keep this excerpt subordinate to the paper stage. Reveal procedural labels only on their supplied global word cues; build the final three-word label through W494–W496. No ballot choices, identities, totals, security scores, or rolling counters.
COLOR/LIGHT  Use a warm-white to pale blue-gray gradient, ivory paper, deep navy typography, and restrained coral inspection accents. Add soft contact shadows between retained sheets and a broad radial highlight behind the aperture. Keep the grid, noise, ghost punctuation, and crosshairs faint. No dark-mode excursion or celebratory teal verification state.
ELEMENTS  Three ivory <mg.Card> sheet planes, including one tilt={-2} rear sheet, with three neutral choice-row rules, three empty choice boxes, one blank footer strip, and one inset margin rule: eleven clean graphic primitives total. · Five wide inspection bands labeled only as spoken: 'paper ballots', 'observers', 'audits', 'recounts', and 'publicly verifiable procedures'. · A coral <mg.FocusFrame> aperture, sparse <mg.Marker> registration crosses, and a thin navy baseline connecting the retained stack to its inspection routes. · The recurring ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner, held at the baseline without a teal check or readable vote. · An 880px ghost question mark beneath the stack at 2% opacity, carrying forward the previous question without inventing a metric. · Multi-stop warm-white background, broad radial spotlight, faint <mg.GridBackground>, and low-opacity <mg.Noise>.
WORD SYNC  W475 → Frames 0–4: reveal 'If' on the inherited goal plane. At frame 2, begin the stack's structural spring entrance beneath the coral aperture; complete that entrance with W479.

AVOID  New illustrative SVG heroes, decorative object icons, or hyper-detailed ballot artwork. · Camera scale above 130%, abrupt zooms, or a static slide presentation. · Candidate names, filled choices, real identities, invented ballot totals, hashes, or election-performance metrics. · Treating observers, audits, recounts, and public procedures as interchangeable, universally available, or sufficient to guarantee legitimacy. · Checks implying voter identity, privacy, consent, or an entire election has been verified. · Uncued labels, duplicated narration, local word-index substitutions, or floating-point trigger timestamps.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_25: A floating coral inspection reticle searches beneath the name 'Blockchain' for the claim 'more secure.' It exposes an unresolved evidence bracket, not a failure indicator. Repeating the name produces no new evidence. The camera then travels back toward the source to expose seven still-unlabeled election-requirement bays.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  A technology label is not evidence of greater security. Inspect that distinction, then reveal the broader requirements elections demand without implying that blockchain failed a security test.
COMPOSITION  1920x1080, 60fps, 524 frames. Use a light-mode, 1760x850 inspection stage occupying approximately 72% of the canvas. Reserve the top-left for the compact headline 'Blockchain' and optional kicker 'Label versus evidence.' Center a 1640px-wide layered platen with a broad naming band above an open evidence field. Match-cut the preceding audit stage's coral aperture, thin baseline, and small ivory vote tile with its navy mark and clipped coral corner. Keep the tile unchecked and secondary. A larger requirements envelope sits behind the platen, initially mostly concealed. This is an investigation surface, not a terminal, ledger table, or comparison dashboard.
CAMERA  Use one continuous <mg.CameraRig>. Begin at 100% with contextual space around the platen; its structural entrance starts at frame 2 using spring damping 14 and stiffness 160, with the hero and 'Blockchain' readable by W497's end, frame 27. Across W498–W499, push to a tight 150% macro framing of the label/evidence boundary while tracking the reticle downward; complete the push by frame 97. Keep the bracket and claim legible at that framing. Across W502–W505, follow a short right-to-left rescan of the naming band, finishing by frame 233. During the following pause, drift subtly toward the slab's source edge. Across W506–W507, continue right to left while pulling to 100%, revealing the complete rear envelope by frame 319. Across W508–W510, ease to 105% over its open interior. On W511–W512, reframe to 100% as seven bays arrive, completing by frame 474. Frames 475–523 retain all seven bays with a barely perceptible lateral drift into the next shot's shared system field.
TYPE  Use premium navy grotesk typography: approximately 40px headline, 112px naming-band label, 82px 'more secure,' and 26px supporting captions. Reveal labels as complete phrases rather than typewriter text. 'Blockchain' settles by frame 27. Begin 'more secure' at W500 and make the complete phrase legible by frame 108, then finish its bracket emphasis by W501's end, frame 131. Reveal the envelope label 'For elections' by frame 319. On W512, set 'much harder' as a restrained envelope-edge caption, not a score or verdict. Preserve the seven bays as blank surfaces.
COLOR/LIGHT  Use a multi-stop warm-white, ivory, and pale blue-gray background with a broad radial spotlight behind the evidence field. Navy typography and hairline rules provide structure. Coral is reserved for the inherited aperture and label-to-evidence boundary, never a failure alarm. Give overlapping cards soft contact shadows, the grid approximately 4% opacity, and noise approximately 2%. Keep the scene light throughout; no teal verification state.
ELEMENTS  One oversized, layered <mg.Card tilt={-2}> platen with a naming band, fine separating rule, and spacious evidence field; flatten the tilt gently during inspection. · A coral <mg.FocusFrame> inherited from the previous shot, functioning as an inspection aperture without an illustrated magnifying glass or optical distortion. · The exact stage labels 'Blockchain' and 'more secure'; place a small 'Evidence required' caption beside an empty, neutral bracket. · A broad rear envelope containing seven equally weighted blank inspection bays in two staggered rows. Reserve all seven requirement labels for the next shot. · An unchecked ivory vote tile, thin navy baseline, <mg.GridBackground>, low-opacity <mg.Noise>, sparse <mg.Marker> registration crosses, and restrained layered shadows. No illustrative entity SVG or numerical display.

pipelineLogs.detail:

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_26: A requirements loom: seven obligations depend on the same election system without any one standing in for the others. Open inspection apertures express questions still to be assessed, not failure or certification. Use only typography, cards, paths, and system conduits; no illustrative entity SVG.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Show seven equally necessary election requirements as one unresolved system, not as a sequence of blockchain capabilities or verified outcomes.
COMPOSITION  1920x1080 at 60fps; 706 frames. A 1760x860 light-mode requirements loom occupies approximately 73% of the canvas. Reserve the top-left for the compact headline 'Election requirements' and kicker 'Illustrative system model.' Expand the inherited seven empty inspection bays into seven large staggered pills: four across the upper row, three across the lower row, surrounding an open shared system field. All pills share height, typography, stroke weight, and unresolved aperture treatment. Fine curved conduits connect each pill independently to the shared field; never connect them into a sequential chain.
CAMERA  Use one continuous <mg.CameraRig>. Start at zoom 1.0 with the inherited envelope fully legible. At frame 3, expand the seven unlabeled bays using restrained springs with damping 14 and stiffness 160; settle by W516's spokenEndFrame 52. Across W517–W525, ease to zoom 1.15 and track right to left across the upper row: accurate counting, voter authentication, ballot secrecy, resistance to coercion. By W526, drift down to the lower-left accessibility pill; track smoothly across auditability to the lower-right security pill through W530. This row-following move follows narration, not data flow. On W531–W532, pull back to zoom 1.0 as the coral frame encloses the complete loom, settling by frame 658. Frames 659–705 hold the completed overview with a subtle lateral ambient drift; no new information. Keep all camera scales within 100–115%.
TYPE  Use a premium navy grotesk with generous spacing: approximately 44px headline, 22px kicker, and 36px pill labels. Give every requirement equal weight; wrap longer labels rather than shrinking them. Empty pills contain no advance labels, numbers, or placeholders. Reveal each label with a short clipped baseline rise and opacity lift driven by its aligned global word cues; append words only as spoken. No rolling metrics, checkmarks, or color-coded scores.
COLOR/LIGHT  Light mode throughout. Blend warm ivory #F7F4ED through pale blue-gray #E8EEF1 with a soft white radial spotlight. Use navy #172B3A typography, muted slate conduits, and restrained coral #E77D70 for the inherited reticle and collective focus frame. Noise and grid remain barely visible. No teal verification state, red failure state, neon glow, or dark-mode transition.
ELEMENTS  Seven equally weighted ivory pills with exact labels revealed only during their spoken phrases: 'accurate counting', 'voter authentication', 'ballot secrecy', 'resistance to coercion', 'accessibility', 'auditability', and 'security against large-scale attacks.' Set the final label on two lines. · An open shared field with seven independent curved bezier conduits and seven unfilled status apertures. Small neutral rectangular packets travel linearly left to right toward the apertures, then stop without checks. · The inherited thin navy baseline, coral inspection reticle, and small ivory vote tile with navy mark and clipped coral corner. Keep the tile parked at the baseline edge as a continuity anchor, never inside a requirement or in a verified state. · A thin coral <mg.FocusFrame> that ultimately encloses all seven obligations without closing their individual status brackets. · A warm multi-stop gradient, broad radial spotlight behind the shared field, faint <mg.GridBackground>, subtle <mg.Noise>, and sparse architectural <mg.Marker> registration crosses. pipelineLogs.message: Shot_27: An insert can fit locally without completing the surrounding structure. Use ten clean native 2D paths for this conceptual geometry, not an illustrative object SVG. pipelineLogs.message: Shot_29: An unscored bento dossier: three equally weighted conditions must remain intact together. The coral line is a shared boundary, and the open apertures express unresolved requirements without declaring failure. No illustrative SVG is needed.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Present ballot secrecy, security, and public trust as three concurrent, unresolved conditions—not scores or trade-offs. Preserve the sentence's continuing thought and prepare the spatial opening for the next shot's database reveal.
COMPOSITION  1920x1080, 60fps, 422 frames. Use a light-mode 1760x850 dossier stage centered below a compact top-left headline, 'Conditions to preserve'. pipelineLogs.message: Shot_21: An information trajectory, not a performance chart: a tile changes upstream, then the ledger faithfully retains that changed pattern. The unresolved coral tether marks the discrepancy before entry; local teal outlines mark only correspondence after entry. Use cards, paths, brackets, and typography, with no illustrative object SVG.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  A hypothetical upstream alteration shows the boundary between preserving an arriving record and preserving the voter's original intent: the ledger retains the altered pattern without resolving its source discrepancy.
COMPOSITION  Render 1920x1080 at 60fps for 576 frames. Use the designated dark-mode exception: a 1760x860 spatial trajectory stage occupying approximately 73% of the canvas. Reserve top-left for the compact headline 'Before the record' and a 'Hypothetical' kicker. A thin baseline runs left to right from x=210 to x=1710 at y=640. Place a broad server-processing slab at x=280–650, an upstream substitution aperture at x=740, and a vertical ledger-entry boundary at x=1020. Three large retained-record windows occupy x=1120–1700 beneath the collective label 'Illustrative record model.' Keep the original-pattern reference above the source and the altered tile on the rail; their separation must remain readable in the final wide view.
CAMERA  Use one continuous <mg.CameraRig>, constrained to zoom 1.00–1.25. Begin at 1.00 with the full contextual trajectory visible. At W417, push toward the upstream aperture, reaching 1.25 by W421. Follow the moving tile left to right through W422–W427 while keeping the ledger-entry boundary ahead of it until the crossing at W427's end. Continue the follow into the retained-record windows through W432. During W434–W435, ease slightly right to left to recover the coral tether and upstream reference while retaining the storage area. On W436, pull back to 1.00, completing by frame 534 so the source discrepancy, entry boundary, and retained pattern are simultaneously legible. Frames 535–575 gently recenter the boundary toward screen center at constant scale for the next comparison shot.
TYPE  Use crisp off-white grotesk typography: 52px compact headline, 26px kicker, and 28–32px stage labels. Keep the headline screen-anchored while stage labels move with the camera. 'Server processing' and its bracket settle by W415; 'Hypothetical' is fully visible by W417 and remains through the exit. Reveal 'Ledger entry' by W427 and 'Illustrative record model' over the downstream windows by W429. On W434, add the small coral annotation 'Altered upstream' beside the discrepancy tether. Avoid giant decorative numerals, quotation-like rewritten narration, and oversized warning language.
COLOR/LIGHT  Blend #08111F, #122436, and #0A1627 across the dark stage. Use ivory #F3EDE1 for the token, off-white #E8EEF2 for text, muted blue-gray for structural planes, coral #F07869 exclusively for the hypothetical upstream discrepancy, and restrained teal #49B5A8 only for stored-to-arriving-pattern correspondence. Soft source and ledger spotlights separate depth planes; keep the grid and noise barely visible. No red alarm wash or full-scene teal verification.
ELEMENTS  <mg.GridBackground> over a multi-stop midnight-navy gradient, restrained radial spotlights, low-opacity <mg.Noise>, and <mg.Marker> crosshairs at the source, entry boundary, and retention endpoint. · Broad neutral processing slab labeled 'Server processing'; a coral <mg.FocusFrame> inspects its perimeter without showing a successful breach. · Recurring ivory vote tile with a navy geometric mark and clipped coral corner. Pattern A consists of two parallel bars; pattern B uses the same bars rotated into a perpendicular arrangement. These are abstract demonstration patterns, not candidate choices. · An upstream coral substitution aperture and a faint, stationary reference tile preserving pattern A above the source. A fine coral discrepancy tether connects this reference to the altered tile. · Vertical boundary labeled 'Ledger entry' and three oversized retained-record <mg.Card> windows, with subtle alternating tilt no greater than 2 degrees. Each eventually contains pattern B. · Extended downstream retention rail with understated ticks and no infinity symbol. No counter or numerical election data.

AVOID  Illustrative server, malware, lock, phone, or ballot-box SVGs in this shot. · Readable ballot choices, real voter identities, invented hashes, numerical performance axes, or counters. · Showing an actual attack or implying every input is altered. · Interpreting teal correspondence as verified identity, privacy, consent, intent, or election validity. · Treating three retained-record windows as three votes, unanimous network control, or measured replication. · Infinity symbols, permanence guarantees, or claims that changing a blockchain record is impossible. · Camera scale above 130%, cuts between clauses, floating-point timing triggers, or replacement local word indices.

pipelineLogs.message: Shot_28: An inspection lens moves from an overbroad absolute to a precise limitation, then expands its field of view to the surrounding election requirements. The same ribbon remains continuous: the argument is refined, not flipped into a verdict.
pipelineLogs.detail:
PREMISE  Clarify the boundary between rejecting blockchain outright and recognizing that blockchain alone does not solve the hardest election problems. Keep the rejected absolute inseparable from its spoken qualification.
COMPOSITION  Render 1920x1080 at 60fps for 619 frames. A light-mode 1760x850 investigation stage occupies approximately 72% of the canvas. Reserve the top-left for the compact headline 'Scope matters'. Below it, build one continuous inspection ribbon on a 1600px horizontal rail with three connected spatial features: an opening qualifier bracket, a narrow movable scope lens, and a broad election-context aperture. These are windows onto one system, not separate cards. The seven inherited requirement tabs sit unchanged and unresolved inside the context aperture. Use two closely spaced depth bands on the same rail: the rejected formulation recedes while the accurate formulation advances. Keep text supporting-scale, fully legible, and subordinate to the oversized stage geometry.
